Section: Chivalry.value:
There are 10 Chivalry abilities, most of which use MP, and some of which have cooldowns (CD). Some are magic buffs, but have no charge time (CT). Two are single target weapon skills, usable with any weapon or unarmed, that deal damage based on Attack and Strength.
In Vanilla mode:
The costs of Resist Break and Magic Break revert to 14 MP.
Armor Boost and Resist Boost revert to single target, but not self, and 1 turn duration.
Power Wall and Magic Wall revert to 6 MP cost, and self only.
Reprisal Aura reverts to single target.
Entrench reverts to no MP cost.
Crystal Form reverts to no MP cost, and no Threat increase.

Section: Wild Arts.value:

In Vanilla mode:

Hew's CT cost reverts to 50 CT.
Balm's CT cost reverts to 50 CT.
Odor Deposit's CT cost reverts to 50 CT. Its cooldown reverts to 4 CD.
There is no Rigid Stance ability.

Section: Beatmaker.value:
There are 10 Beatmaker abilities, most of which self-inflict the Encore Debuff, and either cost AP to deal damage based on Attack and Strength, or cost MP to have magical effects based on Mind or Spirit, with no charge time (CT).
In Vanilla mode:
Beat Roll's damage scaling reverts to 0.006 Str instead of 0.0075 Str.
Rhythm Break reverts to 3 AP cost instead of 4 AP, single target instead of multi-target, and -30% damage/healing penalty instead of -35%.
Crescendo's bonus damage per Buff reverts to 50 + 0.5 Str instead of 60 + 0.6 Str.
Mana Song's base MP Restoration reverts to 9 instead of 10.
Resistance Style reverts to Attack Style, a stance which inflicts the Armor Down Debuff on hit. The user takes 35% more physical damage instead of a -3 AP cost per turn.
Defense Style reverts to Defense Style (vanilla), dealing 35% less physical damage instead of a -3 AP cost per turn.

Section: Skills.value:
Total LP to master: 28
Mastery also requires learning 20 Monster Magic abilities. Each character learns each ability when a monster uses it, if the character is alive, and is a Scholar (with innate passive Learning), or has the Learning passive skill set, or has a Learner's Pin accessory equipped. You don't have to be the Monster Magic's target, but if you are, you have to survive the hit. You learn the ability immediately, so you don't have to survive the fight or win. You can't learn Monster Magic abilities from other party members using them.

There are 10 Time Magic abilities, all of which are single target or self-only magic that use MP, and usually have charge time (CT).
In Vanilla mode:
Dust's MP cost reverts to 16 MP.
Stability's MP cost reverts to 10 MP.
Rewind's MP cost reverts to 24 MP.
Quick's costs revert to 40 MP and 40 CT, and its effect reverts to making the two actions instant, with no CT.

Description.value:
A Bloody Seed is a key item that grows into a Blood Carrot when planted in the garden in Capital Sequoia.
Witchlings in Castle Sequoia have a 10% chance to drop Bloody Seeds.
A Bloody Seed takes 30 minutes of play time to grow into a Blood Carrot. Using the Watering Can reduces the time to 15 minutes. Defeat the Blood Carrot to obtain a Life Line sword, and a Secret Veggie, one of the three ingredients in Nan's Secret Recipe. The Blood Carrot remains planted until you defeat it.

Description.value:
The Cerulean Book is a key item found in The Depths. It's in a chest on the seafloor, west and slightly north of Sara Sara Bazaar, or east and slightly north of the Europa Shrine in the Jidamba Tangle.
The Cerulean Book is one of the three items needed to enter the Sequoia Athenaeum in Tall, Tall Heights. The other two items are the Vermillion Book and the Viridian Book.
A librarian in the Sequoia Athenaeum, in an unlocked hidden room behind the top of the frozen waterfalls, gives a clue to the Cerulean Book's location: "The Cerulean Book was lost near a wrecked whip below the Deep Sea, in The Depths."

Description.value:
A Colony Seed is a key item that grows into a Colonizer when planted in the garden in Capital Sequoia.
Wrensouls in Tall, Tall Heights and Icy Wings in Slip Glide Ride both have a 10% chance to drop Colony Seeds.
A Colony Seed takes 25 minutes of play time to grow into a Colonizer. Using the Watering Can reduces the time to 13 minutes. Defeat the Colonizer to obtain a Spore Shooter bow, and a Secret Meat, one of the three ingredients in Nan's Secret Recipe. The Colonizer remains planted until you defeat it.

Description.value:
Daggers are a martial weapon type.
Warriors, Rogues, Wizards, Warlocks, Hunters, Chemists, Ninjas, Nomads, Assassins, Beastmasters, Weavers, and Mimics can equip daggers. Other classes can equip daggers by setting the Equip Dagger passive from the Rogue skill tree, or the Equip All passive from the Mimic skill tree.
Some daggers are internally called "ninja daggers", and boost Evasion instead of Crit Damage. A Ninja's duel wield attack temporarily unequips the off hand weapon for the main hand attack, then vice versa. This prevents two daggers from stacking Crit Damage during a duel wield attack, but allows two daggers to stack Evasion when being attacked. Ninja daggers aren't class restricted, though; characters who can equip daggers can equip all daggers.
All daggers are one-handed.

Description.value:
A Dione Shard is a tool that teleports the party to the hill above the entrance to the Dione Shrine, between the Quintar Reserve and Flyer's Lookout. One shard is consumed each time it's used.
There are four Dione Shards in chests around the Dione Shrine. If you have the Babel Quintar, a Quintar up the stairs from the Race Registration Counter in the Dione Shrine sells Dione Shards for 50 Silver each. If you've ever had a Dione Shard, but don't anymore, the Lost & Found in Capital Sequoia sells a Dione Shard for 87 Silver 50 Copper. It may be more economical to buy an unlimited-use Dione Stone for 4 Gold instead.

Description.value:
A Dione Stone is a tool that teleports the party to the hill above the entrance to the Dione Shrine, between the Quintar Reserve and Flyer's Lookout. It has unlimited uses, so isn't consumed when used.
If you have the Babel Quintar, a Quintar up the stairs from the Race Registration Counter in the Dione Shrine sells Dione Stones for 4 Gold each. There's no benefit to buying more than one.

Description.value:
Dog Bone is a key item.
The Dog Trainer in Delende near the Soiled Den is looking for 3 Dog Bones. Find the 3 Dog Bones and turn them in to receive the Bone Smasher.
One Dog Bone is through the cave immediately east of the Dog Trainer, in the Soiled Den, guarded by the Bone Thief.
Another Dog Bone is on a hill southeast of the Dog Trainer. From a fallen tree trunk south of the Dog Trainer, jump east onto the hill.
Another Dog Bone is in the Indecent Dweller cave. An entrance to the cave is west of the fallen tree trunk.

Description.value:
A Europa Shard is a tool that teleports the party to the middle level of the Europa Shrine in the Jidamba Tangle. One shard is consumed each time it's used.
The Shrine Attendant in the Europa Shrine sells Europa Shards for 30 Silver each. If you've ever had a Europa Shard, but don't anymore, the Lost & Found in Capital Sequoia sells a Europa Shard for 52 Silver 50 Copper. It may be more economical to buy an unlimited-use Europa Stone for 2 Gold instead.

Description.value:
A Fetish Seed is a key item that grows into a Wai-fu when planted in the garden in Capital Sequoia.
Mage Knights, the fifth battle in the Sky Arena in Shoudu Province, have a 10% chance to drop Fetish Seeds.
A Fetish Seed takes 15 minutes of play time to grow into a Wai-fu. Using the Watering Can reduces the time to 8 minutes. Defeat the Wai-fu to obtain a Cosplay Garb light armor, and a Secret Herb, one of the three ingredients in Nan's Secret Recipe. The Wai-fu remains planted until you defeat it.

Description.value:
The Forgotten Key is a key item that unlocks the doors in the ruins in The Deep Sea southwest of Jidamba Tangle.
It is found in the Deep Sea, in an underwater burrow guarded by Flesh Eaters. Swim west from the Sequoia to find Flesh Eaters hiding in holes in the seafloor. Defeat or evade the Flesh Eaters to enter their burrow.
Most of the ruins can be entered without the Forgotten Key, but one ruin requires the key. Unlocking that ruin gives access to the Soul Keeper sword and a Deep Sea Scrap.

Description.value:
A Gaea Shard is a tool that teleports the party to the roof of the Gaea Shrine in Capital Sequoia. One shard is consumed each time it's used.
There are four Gaea Shards in chests in the Gaea Shrine. The Shrine Attendant in the Gaea Shrine sells Gaea Shards for 10 Copper each. If you've ever had a Gaea Shard, but don't anymore, the Lost & Found in Capital Sequoia sells a Gaea Shard for 17 Copper. It may be more economical to buy an unlimited-use Gaea Stone for 2 Silver instead.

Description.value:
A Ganymede Shard is a tool that teleports the party to the roof of the Ganymede Shrine between Shoudu Province and Flyer's Crag. One shard is consumed each time it's used.
The Shrine Attendant in the Ganymede Shrine sells Ganymede Shards for 3 Silver each. If you've ever had a Ganymede Shard, but don't anymore, the Lost & Found in Capital Sequoia sells a Ganymede Shard for 5 Silver 25 Copper. It may be more economical to buy an unlimited-use Ganymede Stone for 1 Gold instead.

Description.value:
A Gourmet Seed is a key item that grows into a Gourmet when planted in the garden in Capital Sequoia.
Pangolions in the fields of Shoudu Province have a 10% chance to drop Gourmet Seeds.
A Gourmet Seed takes 15 minutes of play time to grow into a Gourmet. Using the Watering Can reduces the time to 8 minutes. Defeat the Gourmet to obtain a Fairy's Crown light hat, and a Secret Veggie, one of the three ingredients in Nan's Secret Recipe. The Gourmet remains planted until you defeat it.

Home Point Stone is a tool that teleports the party to their Home Point. It has unlimited uses, so isn't consumed when used.

If the party hasn't set a Home Point yet, the Home Point Stone teleports the party to the starting position in Spawning Meadows.

Description.value:
The Luxury Key is a key item described as unlocking the luxury shop store room in Capital Sequoia.
Once you've entered the store room and left the area, a thief will spawn in the alley behind the luxury shop. The thief will give you the Luxury Key; apparently, you've foiled his planned burglary.
The requirement to enter the store room before getting the Luxury Key contradicts the Luxury Key's described purpose. That makes the Skeleton Key the only way in. The Luxury Key is only useful for archive completion.

Description.value:
A Mars Shard is a tool that teleports the party to the roof of the Mars Shrine in Poko Poko Desert. One shard is consumed each time it's used.
After you obtain the Mars Stone, the Lost & Found in Capital Sequoia sells a Mars Shard for 3 Copper if you don't currently have a Mars Shard. Buying one is necessary if you want to complete your Archive, but it's more economical to use the Mars Stone instead.

Description.value:
A Mercury Shard is a tool that teleports the party to the roof of the Mercury Shrine between Spawning Meadows and Seaside Cliffs. One shard is consumed each time it's used.
The Shrine Attendant in the Mercury Shrine sells Mercury Shards for 30 Copper each. If you've ever had a Mercury Shard, but don't anymore, the Lost & Found in Capital Sequoia sells a Mercury Shard for 52 Copper. It may be more economical to buy an unlimited-use Mercury Stone for 10 Silver instead.

Description.value:
A Neptune Shard is a tool that teleports the party to the inside of the Neptune Shrine in the Deep Sea between Sara Sara Bazaar and The Sequoia. One shard is consumed each time it's used.
The Shrine Attendant in the Neptune Shrine sells Neptune Shards for 50 Silver each. If you've ever had a Neptune Shard, but don't anymore, the Lost & Found in Capital Sequoia sells a Neptune Shard for 87 Silver 50 Copper. It may be more economical to buy an unlimited-use Neptune Stone for 4 Gold instead.

Description.value:
To obtain a map of the Poko Poko Desert, you need to trade a Shoudu Stew with a man by the docks. Shoudu Stew can be purtchased from a Stew seller by the Shoudu Province docks.
You can reach Shoudu Province by land or sea, but you will need a Ferry Pass if you don't want to walk.
Land: Travel east from Cobblestone Crag, through Okimoto N.S., until you reach Shoudu Province.
Sea: You will need to obtain a Ferry Pass, which can be done in two ways.
1. Acquire 15 crystals and talk to the Ticket Agent in Sara Sara Bazaar, in the shop between the two docks. This will be very challenging if you are on a first playthrough.
2. A worried mother can be found near the northeast exit of the Bazaar. If you can find her son in Poko Poko Desert then she will reward you with a Ferry Pass. He can be found by taking the eastern exit into the desert and following the dirt colored winding path through the cliffs, without falling down into the sands below. Eventually you will reach a dead end where the boy is, who will run back to his mother afterwards.

Description.value:
A Poseidon Shard is a tool that teleports the party to the roof of the Poseidon Shrine on the cliff behind the Salmon Shack in Salmon River. One shard is consumed each time it's used.
The Salmon Shack reception awards you a Poseidon Shard as a participation prize each time you complete the Salmon Sprint. The Shrine Attendant in the Poseidon Shrine sells Poseidon Shards for 20 Copper each. If you've ever had a Poseidon Shard, but don't anymore, the Lost & Found in Capital Sequoia sells a Poseidon Shard for 35 Copper. It may be more economical to buy an unlimited-use Poseidon Stone for 15 Silver instead.

Description.value:
The Rampart Key is a key item that unlocks a door on the west side of the Castle Ramparts.
It is found in The Deep Sea, east of Seaside Cliffs and south of Cobblestone Crag, visible under a pane of glass in the seafloor. Swim west from the glass along the seafloor to find a hidden, north-facing entrance to the corridor leading to the key.
Unlocking the Castle Ramparts door gives access to an isolated room in Castle Sequoia containing a Decapitator axe and the Castle Sequoia Map.

The Seal can also be traded in the Jade Cavern to receive the unique class armor, Reaper Mail.

Description.value:
Used in crafting. Silver Dust is required for upgrading the Craftwork gear into Silver gear.
Silver Dust is used to make:
Silver Staff
Silver Wand
Silver Pages
Silver Shield
Silver Crown
Silver Cape
Silver Dust is found in the following locations:
Rolling Quintar Fields x 1 (Hidden underground, southwest of quintar enthusiast's house.)
Quintar Nest x 1 (South of where you fall into Quintar Nest from above, almost at water level.)
Quintar Sanctum x 2 (One found on the northeast of the lower section, requires bouncing up from mushrooms. Other is found near the first dust, but much higher up. More mushroom bouncing required. Just west of a sign saying "Qwei".)
Capital Jail x 2 (One in the East Wing, first door. Other is in the Dark Wing, second door on the right.)
Cobblestone Crag x 1 (Between 2 waterfalls, southeast of Capital Courtyard.)
Okimoto N.S. x 2 (One found during the ascent of the cliff face, around halfway up to the left of a steep ladder of beams. Other is found on the second floor of the compound, in the southwest room.)
Greenshire Reprise x 1 (Center of the area, left of the middle bridge in the group of three. In a crevice between two trees.)
Poko Poko Desert x 2 (One south of Mars Shrine, in a destroyed building. Another south of Ancient Reservoir, on top of a destroyed building.)
Sara Sara Bazaar x 2 (Both underwater at the end of the right pier. Arrrr.)
Sara Sara Beach x 5 (Three found on the east section of the beach along the cliffs, near the Ibek's Cave homepoint. One found on a cliff on the west part of the beach, west of the Bazaar. One found in the large green section in the northwest part of the Beach, just north of the small pool.)
Ancient Reservoir x 1 (Right side of the Boss chamber, where the goats live. You will likely pass it on your way out.)
Capital Sequoia x 1 (sold by the Lost & Found shop)

Description.value:
Used in crafting. Silver Ingot is required for upgrading the Craftwork gear into Silver gear.
Silver Ingot is used to make:
Silver Katana
Silver Spear
Silver Scythe
Silver Bow
Silver Helm
Silver Mail
Silver Ore is found in the following locations:
Rolling Quintar Fields x 1 (Hidden underground, to the east of the topmost point of the large mesa just outside the Capital. There is a group of 3 trees, and a 4th in a pit. Entrance is in the west side of the pit.)
Quintar Nest x 1 (West of the pond circled by Brutish Quintar, near the south entrance to Jojo Sewers.)
Quintar Sanctum x 2 (One on northwest edge of the lower section, just above where the water ends. One on northwest part of lower section, near a cluster of bouncy mushrooms.)
Capital Jail x 2 (Both found in the south wing, 3rd door on the left and 4th door on the right.)
Capital Pipeline x 1 (At the mid-section where passage is blocked by crates, directly south of capital pipeline homepoint.)
Okimoto N.S. x 2 (One found within the compound, on a pillar to the right of the pond. One found on the second floor of the compound, connected to the southwest room.)
Greenshire Reprise x 1 (On the southeast tip, where Delende is visible to the south and Capital wall is visible ot the east.)
Poko Poko Desert x 2
Sara Sara Bazaar x 2 (Both underwater at the end of the right pier. Arrrr.)
Sara Sara Beach x 6 (Three on the east section of the beach along the cliffs, near the Ibek's Cave homepoint. One on the sand on west part of the beach, just in front of the large green section. One on the beach, up against the southwest side of the giant cube. One on an island west of the Master Dervish.)
Ancient Reservoir x 1 (East side, through a door leading to waterway/underpass from the room with moving crates. From entrance take the stairs down to homepoint, then follow around to right.)

Description.value:
A Sketchy Seed is a key item that grows into a Weed when planted in the garden in Capital Sequoia.
Hobos in the Jojo Sewers have a 10% chance to drop Sketchy Seeds. Also, the Lost & Found in Capital Sequoia sells 2 Sketchy Seeds, 1 at a time, for 70 Copper each.
A Sketchy Seed takes 5 minutes of play time to grow into a Weed. Using the Watering Can reduces the time to 3 minutes. Defeat the Weed to obtain a Secret Herb, one of the three ingredients in Nan's Secret Recipe. The Weed remains planted until you defeat it.

Description.value:
A Spore Seed is a key item that grows into a Shroomy when planted in the garden in Capital Sequoia.
Yammas around the Okimoto N.S. have a 10% chance to drop Spore Seeds.
A Spore Seed takes 12 minutes of play time to grow into a Shroomy. Using the Watering Can reduces the time to 6 minutes. You can learn the Monster Magic Regenerate from the Shroomy. Defeat the Shroomy to obtain a Magic Finder accessory, and a Secret Meat, one of the three ingredients in Nan's Secret Recipe. The Shroomy remains planted until you defeat it.

Description.value:
A Tear Seed is a key item that grows into a Red Onion when planted in the garden in Capital Sequoia.
Sabertooths in Tall, Tall Heights have a 5% chance to drop Tear Seeds. Also, two Tear Seeds are in chests in Tall, Tall Heights, and another Tear Seed is in a chest in the Northern Cave.
A Tear Seed takes 20 minutes of play time to grow into a Red Onion. Using the Watering Can reduces the time to 10 minutes. Defeat the Red Onion to obtain an Onion Gi medium armor. The Red Onion remains planted until you defeat it.

Description.value:
The Treasure Finder is a key item that displays nearby unopened treasure chests on your mini-map.
The Treasure Finder is found in The Deep Sea, below the north edge of Tall, Tall Heights. Answer all 8 Quizzards correctly to unlock the door leading to the Treasure Finder.
There are 8 questions to answer in total:
What item did you need to collect several of to get the map of Seaside Cliffs?
Clamshells
Why didn't Orchard and Little H want you to go near Castle Sequoia?
They were afraid of punishment.
Which job is granted by the crystal found in Capital Sequoia?
Beatsmith
Of the following eyeballs, which does the Quintar Enthusiast hate the most?
Fiendish
How many participants are present during the Salmon Run?
16
How many crystals are currently required to obtain a Quintar Pass?
7
What's the behavior sequence?
Overalls
In which of these regions can you obtain the Guaba summon?
Salmon Bay
Once you obtain the Treasure Finder, it's automatically active whenever the mini-map displays.

Description.value:
A Triton Shard is a tool that teleports the party to the roof of the Triton Shrine in Tall, Tall Heights. One shard is consumed each time it's used.
The Shrine Attendant in the Triton Shrine sells Triton Shards for 50 Silver each. If you've ever had a Triton Shard, but don't anymore, the Lost & Found in Capital Sequoia sells a Triton Shard for 87 Silver 50 Copper. It may be more economical to buy an unlimited-use Triton Stone for 1 Gold 50 Silver instead.

Description.value:
A Tuber Seed is a key item that grows into a Dye Khan when planted in the garden in Capital Sequoia.
Cappers in the Salmon River have a 15% chance to drop Tuber Seeds. Also, two Tuber Seeds are in chests in Capital Sequoia, in the Gardener's Shed. The Gardener's Key in the nearby hedge maze unlocks the Gardener's Shed.
A Tuber Seed takes 10 minutes of play time to grow into a Dye Khan. Using the Watering Can reduces the time to 5 minutes. Defeat the Dye Khan to obtain a Secret Veggie, one of the three ingredients in Nan's Secret Recipe. The Dye Khan remains planted until you defeat it.

Description.value:
The Vermillion Book is a key item found in the Chalice of Tar. It's in a chest on a rock in the tar, reachable through the cave next to the Mimic's Alcove.
The Vermillion Book is one of the three items needed to enter the Sequoia Athenaeum in Tall, Tall Heights. The other two items are the Viridian Book and the Cerulean Book.
A librarian in the Sequoia Athenaeum, in an unlocked hidden room behind the top of the frozen waterfalls, gives a clue to the Vermillion Book's location: "The Vermillion Book was lost east of Tall, Tall Heights, atop The Chalice of Tar."

Description.value:
A Watery Seed is a key item that grows into a Water Carrot when planted in the garden in Capital Sequoia.
Merhorses and Sea Salamanders in The Deep Sea both have a 10% chance to drop Watery Seeds.
A Watery Seed takes 30 minutes of play time to grow into a Water Carrot. Using the Watering Can reduces the time to 15 minutes. Defeat the Water Carrot to obtain an Aura Focus wand, and a Secret Veggie, one of the three ingredients in Nan's Secret Recipe. The Water Carrot remains planted until you defeat it.

Description.value: Capital Sequoia is the largest city of Sequoia. It's a hub for adventurers and a place to recover from their journeys. To be allowed access to the city, adventurers must find 3 crystals and survive the Trial Caves and Skumparadise. The city sits on top of the cliff north of the Proving Meadows. It's connected to the Capital Courtyard to the south, the Rolling Quintar Fields to the east, and Greenshire Reprise to the west. The Jojo Sewers are below the city. The Grand Master's home, Castle Sequoia, lies north, at the other side of the maze and separated from the rest of the city by a moat, requiring an Ibek to cross.

Section: Garden.value:
The following seeds can be planted in the garden in the northeast of Capital Sequoia. Talk to the gardener to plant one in one of the six plots. Section: Maze.value:
Some of the walls in the maze can be walked through. You can use the nudge camera buttons to see them more easily. Some of them require jumping to get into the hedge. See the screenshot for paths you can walk through. A J is a place you may need to jump, and a C is a chest. The chest next to the crate allows you to jump on top of the hedges to make it easier. Alternatively, once you can jump higher, you can skip the maze by jumping on top of the hedges to clear the maze.
Defeat all the enemies in the maze for a hint for Secret Boomer Society.

Section: Broken Bridge.value: A small canyon splits northern Delende into two halves, of which the easiest way to get across had been destroyed in some unknown incident. An adventuring party would now have to take a detour towards the Pale Grotto, but this might not be that much of an inconvenience, as a crystal is rumored to be within. A man on the eastern side has figured out a novel solution to the problem of the broken bridge, if you decide to indulge his request.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Connected regions.value:
Spawning Meadows: To the southwest. A new adventuring party is likely climbing from the Spawning Meadows to reach Delende.
Seaside Cliffs: To the southeast. There are two entrances to the Seaside Cliffs from Delende. If your party's goal is to reach Mercury Shrine, it is recommended to enter from the southwestern entrance and hug the western cliffs as much as possible, until you are able to make the climb to the shrine. There may be a crystal somewhere within the Cliffs.
The Pale Grotto: A vast cave network that stretches beneath Greenshire Reprise above. A crystal is rumored to be within.
See Soiled Den entry above.
Mercury Shrine: To the south. From the top of the climb from Spawning Meadows, there's a tree immediately to the east. Use that tree to jump south onto the hill. Go west around the hill to reach the Mercury Shrine, part of the Fast Travel network.
Proving Meadows: The goal of an adventuring party new to the land of Sequoia. It acts as a home base before the trek into the Trial Caves, though a guard at the entrance of the gauntlet will demand that your party finds 3 crystals before allowing them to pass.
See Gran's Hut entry above.
Yamagawa M.A.: A mountain to the west, with Gran's Hut marking the entrance to this region. A crystal is rumored to be found within the mountains.

There is two shops, for weapons and armor, and lodging within the hut as well.

Section: Hobo Hideout.value:
A cave populated by Indecent Hobos on the lower section that will defend themselves against an adventuring party seeking to chase them down. A Scholar could learn something useful from observing them, for they may have learned a skill that's a secret to the rest of Sequoia. It is likely that one of them may have stolen one of the dog bones as well.
To reach the upper levels of the Hobo Hideout to cross the bridge network that ultimately leads the party towards Gran's Hut and Yamagawa M.A., an adventuring party will have to jump across a tree near the Broken Bridge. A Scholar can be seen observing the region from atop this tree.

Section: Charge Time.value:
Charge Time (also known as CT) is just like TT, except it applies to how long it takes to use an ability. An ability which costs CT is not used right away. Instead, when the ability is selected, a countdown is set equal to the ability's CT. When it hits zero, that fighter finally gets to use the ability. Afterwards, their turn ends and their TT Counter resets.
If an ability's CT is low enough, you may have noticed you usually get to use it right away anyway. But don't forget that even in this case, you still need to wait longer for your next turn.
Note: The Order Window on bottom of the screen will display when your abilities will complete.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified
sources.locator: House of The Know-It-All Ducks > Crit. Damage Bonus

Section: Crit. Damage Bonus.value:
When a piece of equipment provides Crit. Damage Bonus, this amount is flat damage added to any attack that lands as a crit. This bonus damage does not take into account your Crit. Damage Percent, but it is also not reduced by the target's Defense.
For example, let's say you have a Crit. Damage Percent of 50%, and Crit. Damage Bonus of 25, and you land a crit using an attack that deals 100 damage. First, without Crit. damage Bonus, your attack will deal 150 damage. This will be reduced by the target's Defense, perhaps down to something like 110. And then your Crit. Damage Bonus will be added to it, resulting in 135 damage. The final result, however, will take into account things like increased or reduced Physical Damage due to status effects.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified
sources.locator: House of The Know-It-All Ducks > Crit. Resist

Section: Crit. Resist.value:
Crit. Resist reduces the amount of damage taken from attacks that land as critical hits. The amount of damage reduced is equal to a percent of the different between a normal hit and a critical hit.
For example, if an attack would do 100 damage normally, and 200 damage as a critical hit, then having 50% Crit. Resist would reduce the amount of crit damage taken from this attack to 150. Having 100% Crit. Resist essentially makes critical hits hurt just the same as normal hits.

sources.locator: House of The Know-It-All Ducks > Damage Categories

Section: Damage Categories.value:
There are several different categories of damage: "Physical Damage", "Magical Damage", "Damage", and "Healing". When a status effect, passive or piece of equipment increases or decreases a specific category of damage, it might pay off to understand explicitly which abilities are affected.
"Physical Damage" refers to damage (not healing) dealt by any ability that is a "basic attack", a "Weapon skill", or a weapon type skill (for example, "Dagger skill").
"Magical Damage" refers to damage (not healing) dealt by any ability that is "magic". That is, the ability has "magic" in its description.
"Healing" refers to healing given by any ability that heals, regardless of whether the ability is physical or magical.
"Damage" refers to damage dealt by any ability that is not a healing ability, regardless of whether it is physical or magical.
"Damage/Healing" refers to all damage or healing of any kind.

sources.locator: House of The Know-It-All Ducks > Damage-per-turn Resistance

Section: Damage-per-turn Resistance.value: Damage per turn based on a percentage of maximum HP sounds extremely powerful against bosses, since their have large HP pools. Unfortunately, almost all bosses have a natural resistance to damage-per-turn status effects. You can verify this for yourself the next time you fight a boss by opening the enemy's info window.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified
sources.locator: House of The Know-It-All Ducks > Damage/Healing-per-turn Status Effects

Section: Damage/Healing-per-turn Status.value:
Damage-per-turn status effects, like Poison and Burn, deal damage to you at the start of each turn while they are applied. They cause damage based on a percentage of your maximum HP.
There are also healing-per-turn status effects, like Regen, that work the same way except they heal you for a percentage of your maximum HP.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified
sources.locator: House of The Know-It-All Ducks > Defense vs. Resistance

Section: Defense vs. Resistance.value:
If an ability is a "basic attack", a "Weapon skill", or a weapon type skill (for example, "Dagger skill"), then the damage it deals will consider the target's Defense.
If an ability is "magic" (that is, the ability has "magic" in its description), then damage it deals will consider the target's Resistance.
If an ability is neither a weapon skill nor magic (for example, Chi Burst), then its damage will ignore the target's Defense/Resistance entirely.
If an ability is a healing ability, then it will ignore the target's Defense/Resistance regardless of whether the ability is physical or magical.
There are some exceptions to these rules, but such exceptions are always listed in the ability's description.

Section: Flame Respawning.value:
For a flame to respawn, you must both leave the current region AND go far enough away from its spawn point. So switching regions isn't enough to make a flame respawn if the flame's spawn point is still nearby.
Also, needless to say, boss flames don't respawn. Once you kill a boss, it's gone for good.

sources.locator: House of The Know-It-All Ducks > Gold Loss on Defeat

Section: Gold Loss on Defeat.value:
Upon defeat or giving up a battle, you drop a bit of Gold. The amount your drop is equal to the amount of Gold that would be rewarded by the remaining monsters. However, the amount you drop is capped. The cap is based on you party's average level. So if you run into some super high level monsters, you don't need to worry about going bankrupt. There is also another cap: you'll never drop more than 10% of you current gold.
Lastly, you'll never drop anything if you lose to or give up versus a boss.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified
sources.locator: House of The Know-It-All Ducks > Guaranteed Hits vs. Misses

Section: Guaranteed Hits vs. Misses.value:
There exist several statuses and passives which have the effect of granting either guaranteed hits or guaranteed misses. You should know that if an attack is somehow both guaranteed to hit and guaranteed to miss at the same time, the guaranteed miss will take priority and the attack will not hit.
Also, the same rule applies to calculating guaranteed crits and crit immunity. That is, if an attack is both guaranteed to crit and guaranteed to not crit at the same time, the attack will not crit.

sources.locator: House of The Know-It-All Ducks > Percentages

Section: Percentages.value:
When an ability or status description says it adds or subtracts a stat by a percent, the result is additive. When an ability of status description says that is provides "more" or "less" percent of a stat, the result is multiplicative.
For example, if you have 50% crit chance and you equip something that says "Crit Chance: +20% ", your crit chance becomes 70%. But if you have 50% crit chance and you equip something that says "Crits are given 20% more often", your crit chance becomes 60%.
Furthermore, when stacking bonuses, all flat bonuses are applied first, followed by all additive bonuses, and lastly all multiplicative bonuses.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified
sources.locator: House of The Know-It-All Ducks > Physical Stats

Section: Physical Stats.value:
Each party member has their own Crit. Chance and Crit. Damage stats. These stats only apply to physical abilities. That is, any ability that is a "basic attack", a "Weapon skill", or a weapon type skill (for example, "Dagger skill"). If a physical ability has its own Crit. Chance or Crit. Damage stats, they stack additively with the user's own Crit. Chance and Crit. Damage.
If a non-physical ability has its own Crit. Chance or Crit. Damage stats, then those are the final values, and they will not be changed by the user's own Crit. Chance and Crit. Damage.

sources.locator: House of The Know-It-All Ducks > Threat: Damage

Section: Threat: Damage.value:
Damaging a monster will increase the attacking party member's Threat for that monster. The amount of Threat generated is exactly equal to the amount of damage dealt.
For example, if a party member deals 100 damage to a monster, then that party member generates 100 Threat for the attacked monster.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified
sources.locator: House of The Know-It-All Ducks > Threat: Decay

Section: Threat: Decay.value:
At the start of each monster's turn, their Threat value for each party member will naturally decrease by 20%.
For example, if a party member has generated 200 Threat for a monster, it will reduce to 160 Threat at the start of that monster's next turn. And then, a start of that monster's following turn, it will reduce to 128 Threat, and so on. Notice that the more Threat a party member has generated, the faster it will decay.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified
sources.locator: House of The Know-It-All Ducks > Threat: Healing

Section: Threat: Healing.value:
When a party member uses a healing ability they might generate Threat. You only generate Threat for a monster when healing the party member which is that monster's current top Threat target. The amount of Threat generated depends on how much Threat the party member you're healing already has. To put it precisely, take the percentage of maximum HP that was healed: this is the percentage of the target party member's Threat which will be generated for the user.
For example, let's say a party member has 100/200 HP, has generated 100 Threat for monster A, 200 Threat for monster B, and this party member was the top Threat for both. If they are healed for 50 HP, then the party member that healed them would generated 25 Threat for monster A and 50 Threat for monster B.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified
sources.locator: House of The Know-It-All Ducks > Threat: Missing HP

Section: Threat: Missing HP.value:
While a party member is at for below 50% maximum HP, they will generate threat for every monster automatically at the start of each of that party member's turns. The Threat generated automatically is equal to 50% of the party member's missing HP.
For example, while a party member has 50/200 HP, this will generate 75 Threat for each monster at the start of their turns. On the other hand, while a party member has 125/200 HP, they will not automatically generate any threat at the start of their turn.

Section: Turn Time: Speed.value: A party member's Turn Time is based on the Speed attribute. The higher their Speed, the lower their Turn Time, and thus more turns they get.

sources.locator: House of The Know-It-All Ducks > Turn Time: Status Effects

Section: Turn Time: Status Effects.value: Don't forget: if a status or equipment has the effect of lowering your Turn Time, that is a good thing! Similarly, a status which increases your Turn Time makes you act slower. That is not a good thing.

Section: Variance Stacking.value: When you equip so much Variance that it exceeds 100%, you cannot deal negative damage. Your base is 0, but you have no limit to how high you can go. That means that once you start getting you Variance up past 100% it becomes more optimal.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Essentially, 10% of any LP earned for a class is given to all other party members too for free, as a bonus. This works even if you are not the same class.

Section: Vitality.value: Increasing Vitality will grant a bonus to your Defense. The bonus is multiplicative, so high Vitality complements high Defense. Vitality also helps reduce the amount of damage taken from damage per turn status effects like Poison and Burn.

Section: What does Threat do?.value: Threat determines which of your party members a monster will try to attack. During battle, each party member has their own unique Threat value for each of the monsters. A monster will target whichever party member is the highest Threat value for them.

Section: What is AP?.value: Certain abilities need AP to be used. It always resets at the start of battle and you must accumulate it as you need it.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified
sources.locator: House of The Know-It-All Ducks > What is Turn time?

Section: What is Turn time?.value:
Turn Time (also known as TT) is the amount of time you must wait between each turn.
In battle, each fighter has a number that equals to their TT. Between turns, each fighter's number decrements until someone's number hits zero. When it hits zero, that fighter gets to take their turn. After their turn is done, the number is once again set to their TT.
During battle, you can check the amount until anyone's next turn by navigating to the right from the command menu.

Section: Lookouts.value:
There are three old delapidated lookouts around the desert, and each one holds a Lookout Token. If you collect all three tokens you can return them to an NPC in Sara Sara Bazaar, and they will reward you with the Pyramid Key. This key will grant access to the mysterious pyramid found in the east side of the desert.
Central - You'll need a quintar of some description for this token. Leave the Sara Sara Bazaar by the east exit and head north to the cliff edge. There will be a number of columns for you to jump across to reach a raised area that the tower is connected to.
West - Head north out of the west exit of Sara Sara Bazaar. You will shortly come across the broken wooden tower.
North - AS the name suggests, found in the north of the desert. Heading directly northeast of the Mars Shrine should take you to this tower.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Lost Child.value: The lost child in the desert can be found quite easily by leaving Sara Sara Bazaar through the east exit to the desert. Simply follow the path around to the northeast, without dropping down off of the cliffs. Eventually you will come to a small clearing with the child standing alone.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Points of Interest.value: The desert is huge, with lots to find. Using the interactive map of Poko Poko Desert may be helpful if you reach your wits end looking for something.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Pyramid.value: The pyramid structure found in the east side of the desert, battered by a sandstorm, is the entrance to the Ancient Reservoir. This dungeon, as the name suggests, has many waterways to navigate and connects to the Underpass region. Completing this dungeon will reward you with a new movement mechanic that can really help to open up the world of Sequoia.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Speedy Flames.value: Most flames encountered in the desert are very quick across the ground. If you want to avoid fighting each one you come across it is best to be riding a quintar for the extra speed boost. Some may still be quicker than you but you will be able to maneuver around them much easier, particularly those that charge in a straight line. Quintars can be rented from Sara Sara, including the speedy Desert Quintar.

Section: The Trials.value:
Entrance to Trial Caves is prohibited until you are in possession of three crytals. The 'standard' three found by this point would be Fencer from The Pale Grotto, Shaman from Draft Shaft Conduit, and Scholar from Yamagawa M.A.. That said, it is possible to sequence break and find various other crystals first.
You will be challenged by a Knight at the entrance to demonstrate your strength.

Description.value:
The only way to get up to River Cat's Ego, the large salmon-shaped temple, is by climbing the waterfall that is spilling out of its mouth. It is possible to achieve this on any Salmon, including the timed rental from the Salmon River, but you will have to be quick.
Note: there is another way into River Cat's Ego, which requires the Owl. If you can reach the Nomad's Shrine (via bouncing platforms to the south and west), you can fly off the shrine to reach the mountain behind River Cat's Ego (the giant catfish structure) and maneuver your way to the left side of the catfish's mouth. From just above the entrance, you can jump and fly into its mouth, where it's all shallow water.

Section: Quintar Enthusiast's Cabin.value: The home of a self-proclaimed expert of Quintar on the far northeastern side of the fields. He asks for Quintar eyeballs for some unknown and very likely to be awkward reason, and will give you very useful rewards if you turn in eyeballs of certain Quintar sub-species. However, you may end up incurring his wrath if you happen to hand him one from a protected species...

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Quintar Nest.value: A vast hidden cave, of which the entrance is concealed in a tall rocky outcrop at the western side of the fields. Reaching it will require jumping across several trees and following the outlined path, starting from the west of the Quintar Enthusiast's Cabin. The Enthusiast is especially interested in eyeballs from a species of Quintar that make their home at a lake in the southern section of the nest. The northern section of the nest appears to be a good hiding spot for a crystal to reside in.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Quintar Sanctum.value: Another home of Quintar, located at the very north of the Rolling Quintar Fields. A new adventuring party may need the assistance of a rental Quintar to reach the Sanctum, by using their superior speed to jump across the trees and following the outlined paths starting from the hills directly north of the Quintar Stables. The Sanctum has numerous pink mushrooms that Quintar supposedly love jumping on, though an adventuring party can jump on one and get launched high into the air too. The light of a crystal may be seen near the summit of the Sanctum, but there are rumors of an even higher point in the Sanctum that may be home to a species of Quintar that the Enthusiast has never seen before.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Quintar Stables.value: Right at the entrance of the Rolling Quintar Fields, you can rent a Quintar if you possess a Quintar Pass. As of this time, it has been decreed that you need 7 crystals to rent one, but there may be other methods of procuring a pass (or even a personal Quintar of your own).

Section: Someone's getting fined...value:
To gain access to the Athenaeum you will need to find the three missing library books around the world. The ducks hidden above the entrance, on the frozen water flowing from the building, will provide you with clues to their locations.
Viridian
The Viridian Book is found in the Jidamba Eaclaneya. You can find this book in the underwater sections of the dungeon. Once you have your own Salmon you won't have to worry about the timed sections.
Cerulean
The Cerulean Book is found in The Depths. You can find this book in the trench directly west of Sara Sara Beach. The Treasure Finder Key Item is very useful here, look for a purple and brown chest very close to each other.
Vermillion
The Vermillion Book is found in The Chalice of Tar. You can find the chest on the southwest edge of the tar pool, accessible by scaling the cliffs on the south and entering the cave openings.

Section: Sky Arena.value:
In the north east of Shoudu you can find the Sky Arena, a place for challengers to test their mettle for fabulous prizes. You will need to gather 10 elevator parts in order to use the elevator to reach the arena, these can be found scattered around in purple chests. There are 15 to find, so you will have spares.
The Sky Arena allows one character to take on a string of consecutive fights for great rewards. As this character is fighting solo it is best to stack up your best gear and job combos to enhance your chances of success. You will not be healed after each bout, so a character able to kill foes before they can act or one capable of sustaining itself is advised. The Ribbon reward from fight 7 can be very helpful in 8, 9, and 10 so no harm in taking a break at that point if you need to.
Rewards are either dispensed by the reception area directly underneath the Sky Arena or by unlocking rooms to the west of the reception. You may need to use your platforming skills to reach the back three rooms.

Section: Speedy Octopus.value:
A fast octopus spawns southwest of the Neptune Shrine, near a Sequoia root. It swims in a fixed path, starting southwest when you approach, then south over The Depths, southeast over the shipwreck, then south to its starting point, where it reverses course.
It's faster than the Salmon Cello mount, and only slightly slower than the Golden Quintar, so you may have to approach it from southwest of its starting point, and get in front of it.
If you catch it, you get a Pointy Hat, which lets you inflict longer Debuffs.

Section: The Devourer.value:
This huge shark is located in the section of trench north-east of Jidamba Tangle.
During the battle it will frequently use Amnesia to reset threat levels and Cleanse to remove negative status effects, making it hard to tank.
Victory over this fierce creature will grant you the Assassin's Cloak light armour.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: The Enforcer.value:
Big Squid is sitting in the section of trench south-west of Jidamba Tangle (or north of the summon master in Tall, Tall Heights).
This monster uses damage-over-time effects to cause you pain rather than front-loaded damage, and likes to turtle up and steal your MP while you suffer.
Conquering this foe will award you with the Ghendolf's Ring accessory.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: The Old One.value:
Cthulu can be found in the vaguely star-shaped pool of Depths disconnected from the trench running east-west, found to the north of Tall, Tall Heights.
During the fight the Old One will use the powerful Dark Overture magic, and will also summon Torpedo enemies that will self-destruct with the Explode spell.
When The Old One falls you will be rewarded with Master Material, and accessory that grants all abilities of your current class without needing to learn them.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: The Peacekeeper.value:
This gross deflated thing is found in the section of trench directly east of Dione Shrine.
It is accompanied by four Tentamouth enemies with each absorbing different elements, rendering some area magics less effective during this encounter. They will also attempt to drain your HP with Blood Suck and paralyse you with Wrap.
The Peacekeeper itself is a souped-up version of Canal Beast and will use the powerful Floodgate ability to deal Water damage to your entire party as well as Wrap and Ink Blast to inflict status effects.
When you emerge victorious you will receive a Guardian Angel heavy armour.

Section: Platforming is Fun.value:
It can be done with Owl and Salmon mounts, but the platforming here will involve lots of jumps, gliding, and water - you may find it less frustrating if you've invested the time in acquiring the Golden Quintar via Quintar Breeding. (Your mileage may vary, some find the breeding process more frustrating!)
Progression through the tree, while individual jumps can be challenging, is not too complex. You'll need to swim through the entrance in the south before climbing the water and tree boughs to the highest point. Using the trick of falling in water to keep your saved position on higher ground can be invaluable, but you'll need to remember to switch off of swimming mounts quickly.
Eventually you will head outside to climb some more before finding a very welcome home point. Once safe in the knowledge that you never have to do that again you can enter the room beyond for the boss fight.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Spirit Cage.value: Spirit Cage can be a real handful - this foe hits hard, crits often, and will frequently raise two allies to make things worse. You can alleviate some of the pressure by raising one of its allies yourself - it will not have full health this way and can be dispatched more quickly. This will prevent the other being raised as Spirit Cage will not resurrect one by itself, only both at once.

Section: Judgement.value:
A party of adventurers accost you at several places in the Undercity. Their actions depend on how much money you've given the Hobos in Shoudu Province.
Encountered a hobo, and refused to give money
"You are despicably cheap." Two wizards blast you with Flare and Thunder, then escape.
Gave 1 Copper, or haven't encountered a hobo
"Your contribution so far leaves much to be desired." A ninja and a samurai hit you with weapon skills, then escape.
Gave 1 Silver
"You have contributed sufficiently so far." They leave without battling you.
Gave 1 Gold
"You are marvelously generous!" They restore your HP and MP, then escape.

Section: Strategy.value:
Coyote is the Water elemental summon, and as such using any Water attacks will be detrimental in this fight.
Multi-target attacks are also not recommended, as the Mind's Delusion that accompanies this boss will respond to any damage by casting Death. Coyote will use Atmoshear to confuse your party in an attempt to trigger this Death counter, and in the same vein Mind's Delusion will also cast Insult.
The Samurai passive Unreactable, which prevents counter attacks, could be used to avoid this, as well as many Rogue skills.
If Coyote is defeated before Mind's Delusion then it will use Escape.

Section: Strategy.value:
Ioske is the Earth elemental summon, and as such using any Earth attacks will be detrimental in this fight. Equiping your team with Float gear or casting it during the fight will cause Ioske to use his 50 Gs ability to dispell it, buying you a turn where he is not attempting to attack.
Non-float immunity to Earth can limit his efficacy (ie Gaia Axe).
Ioske is capable of hard-hitting magic and physical attacks, so applying blind can be helpful in cutting the number of buffs required for your team to survive.

Description.value:
Owlbear will always use Hyper Crush on the highest threat if they aren't paralyzed which paralyzes the target for 4 turns, and it won't use it if it had used Hyper Crush within the last 4 turns. Otherwise it will use Blood Spiller (only on Normal Difficulty or higher), Weeping Cry, or Hyper Slam. It won't use Blood Spiller if it has been used within the last 3 turns, it won't use Hyper Slam if it's been used within the last 2 turns, and it won't use Weeping Cry if Weeping Cry has been used within the last 4 turns. It also won't use Weeping Cry if the target has Weep. It also won't use Blood Spiller if the target has bleed. If it can't use any of those attacks then it will just use it's basic Attack.
Upon reaching 70% HP, it will use Owl's Minuet (only on Normal Difficulty or higher) which gives everyone including the Owlbear an effect that gives 100% variance to everything. Upon reaching 50% HP, it will use Stone Skin which applies a buff to itself that gives it 100% more Defense.

Section: Strategy.value:
The Tomb Guard is one the deadliest normal enemies in the entire game. Its stats, combined with the Undead buff makes it an immensely deadly fighter, capable of instantly wiping the entire party if it gets the first turn, which most likely will if your characters aren't fast enough.
Tomb Guards are only encountered in the second and third floors of the Mausoleum, and only attack if their flames are approached too closely. Beware, as their flames move extremely fast.
The Tomb Guard's Blood Spiller is its most dangerous attack, and the one it always uses in its first turn. It hits the entire party, and the damage is further boosted by 35%. It can easily deal enough damage to kill anyone with less than around 800 HP. It can also use Fighter Crush, which can deal over 3000 damage if it crits.
If you're unlucky/crazy enough to fight them, remove the Undead buff with a buff-removing ability like the Warlock's Dispel, and use anything that may afflict them with Power Down to minimize their melee damage.

Section: Strategy.value:
The two Meat enemies should be disposed of quickly to allow you to focus on just the Troll.
Rogue is suggested for this fight as Blind debuff will negate the Troll's physical attacks for a turn.
When at low HP, the Troll will attempt to buff itself to take actions much, much faster. Preparing to burst away the last of its HP is a useful precaution to take, as such frequent attacks can easily end your attempt in the blink of an eye.

Description.value:
See also: Crafting
The Blacksmiths are a series of vendors that will upgrade some of your gear for you. They upgrade Craftwork weapons and armor into Silver, then onto Gold and finally to Diamond. There are five blacksmith shops through the game. When you reach a new one, news of their trade reaches the capital and will also be available there. Explore the world to find dust, ore, and ingots to upgrade all of your gear! These items tend to have high base stat for their tier, without any special abilities.
Silver weapons and armor: All begin available in Capital Sequoia.
Gold armor: Sara Sara Bazaar, bottom tier near the docks.
Gold weapons: Shoudu Province, not far from the docks to the left.
Diamond armor: Tall, Tall Heights, the big building in the center, near Triton Shrine.
Diamond weapons: Jidamba Tangle, southeast corner.
Upgrading a weapon costs:
Silver gear: 3 silver coins, 3 silver materials, plus the Craftwork base.
Gold gear: 30 silver coins, 3 gold materials, plus the Silver base.
Diamond gear: 5 gold coins, 3 diamond materials, plus the Gold base.
Whether the upgrade needs dust, ore, or ingot materials varies by the gear type. These are:
Martial weapons (sword, axe, dagger, rapier), and medium armor use ore.
Exotic weapons (katana, spear, scythe, bow), and heavy armor use ingots.
Caster weapons (staff, wand, book), shields, and light armor use dust.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Location.value:
Location is a set of 3 floats representing x-y-z coordinates. Note that there are approximately 90 memory locations with the same value; only one controls the actual location.
Simple way to find coordinates is to start with the Z value (smallest range):
Go to the tallest convenient place (shrine?)
Start search for Float type, value between 10 and 300
drop down a little / start floating with Owl
Scan for decreased value (set up a hotkey for ease of use, in settings)
Repeat 4+5 until found list is <100 or so
Add all addresses; most should be around the same value. Remove any that aren't.
Freeze the addresses. You should be unable to jump/fall. If not, start over.
Freeze and unfreeze half the addresses at a time, checking if you can jump/fall, remove whatever doesn't work.
You have the Z value!
Browse memory near there - the X and Y are nearby. Similar procedure to verify them.

Section: Craftwork Gear Locations.value:
Weapons
Craftwork Sword - In the Library, on top of the bookshelves. Fall down from chimney above.
Craftwork Spear - In the Maze, on the east side, about halfway up.
Craftwork Wand - In the Maze, in the lower west corner in the dead end.
Craftwork Katana - Top of the agility course where the Ninja trains.
Craftwork Dagger - In the Rogue Hideout, above the Weary Wanderer's Lodge.
Craftwork Axe - Above the House of The Know-It-All Ducks, accessed via the chimney.
Craftwork Pages - Above Weapons "R" Us, in the Wizard Master's room.
Craftwork Bow - Above Armor "4" All, and below the Beatsmith crystal.
Craftwork Rapier - Behind the fence to the right of Magic and Magic Things. Can be accessed by jumping over the fence with Ibek, or by going into the sewers.
Craftwork Scythe - Inside Magic and Magic Things, platform up to it from behind the counter.
Craftwork Staff - In the Red Door Inn, the left room at the back.
Armor
Craftwork Cap - In the back alley behind the Blacksmith.
Craftwork Crown - In the Maze, upper west side.
Craftwork Robe - In the Penguin Pen, under the shelter.
Craftwork Vest - On top of the Red Door Inn, accessed via rooftops.
Craftwork Shield - On top of the Blacksmith building, accessed via rooftops.
Craftwork Helm - Behind the fence to the right of Armor "4" All.
Craftwork Mail - In the Gardener's Hut. Will require Gardener's Key from the Maze, or the Skeleton Key from Sequoia Athenaeum.

Section: Upgrade Tiers.value:
The Craftwork gear can be upgraded 3 times, through the below levels. Progress is gated based on visiting certain areas and speaking to the relevant Blacksmiths:
Silver - Available on reaching the Capital Blacksmith.
Gold - Weaponsmith is found in Shoudu Province, in the building north of the longer, elevated, dock on the left. Armorsmith is found in Sara Sara Bazaar, in the building immediately north of the left dock.
Diamond - Weaponsmith is found in Jidamba Tangle, on the south east of the island. Armorsmith is found in Tall, Tall Heights, in the building west of Triton Shrine.

Section: Crystals In-Game.value:
Crystals are often found at the end of a dungeon or area. When the player first interacts with a Crystal, they receive a new class and have both their HP and MP fully restored.
Afterwards, Crystals can be used similarly to save points to change class, choose templates, change member order or save. However, unlike save points, they cannot be chosen as homepoints to warp to.

Description.value:
The demo for Crystal Project is rather lengthy and gives a great idea of what the game has to offer. Some people online have reported getting 10 or more hours of enjoyment out of the demo alone. The demo does include some dungeons, new classes to unlock, some possible sequence breaking through creative exploration, and even has a few of the later-game optional bosses you can run into and be killed by.
The demo does have some NPCs telling you "You can't go here in the demo" in some places (some of which can be circumvented) and is missing some resources for areas you can get to (like missing battle music in an area the developer didn't expect people would find a way into from the demo).
Save games transfer from the demo to the full title once you have purchased it, though the developer has warned it's possible (though not currently planned) that this could change in the future if the full game receives significant changes.

entities.name: Crystal Project Demo
entities.rawDescription: The demo for Crystal Project is rather lengthy and gives a great idea of what the game has to offer. Some people online have reported getting 10 or more hours of enjoyment out of the demo alone. The demo does include some dungeons, new classes to unlock, some possible sequence breaking through creative exploration, and even has a few of the later-game optional bosses you can run into and be killed by. The demo does have some NPCs telling you "You can't go here in the demo" in some places (some of which can be circumvented) and is missing some resources for areas you can get to (like missing battle music in an area the developer didn't expect people would find a way into from the demo). Save games transfer from the demo to the full title once you have purchased it, though the developer has warned it's possible (though not currently planned) that this could change in the future if the full game receives significant changes.

Description.value:
On starting a game, you are presented with the following options. At any point while playing, you can lower the difficulty from the menu. Once you lower it, you cannot raise it again for this save file unless you enable an assist option.
Easy
For those who would like a more laid-back experience where battles are not the priority. Enemies have less HP and deal less damage to the party.
Normal
The standard experience for those who enjoy RPGs. Battles will be tough but grinding should not be necessary.
Hard
For those who would like an even greater challenge. Battles will be very hard. Grinding will be necessary. Not recommend for first-time players.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Assist Options.value:
A wide variety of assist options are available to you. Once any of these are enabled, they are locked to on for your save file and cannot be disabled. Some, however, let you set their numbers to the defaults (but your save file will still mark that it has been enabled).
Enhanced Home Point:Enables setting up to 3 different Home Points at a time. Earlier parts of the game can often involve a lot of backtracking. Most players may want to enable this option.
Healing Home Point:Enables free, automatic full recovery for the party when interacting with a Home Point. (Note: Once you get your first Shrine Stone, you normally can set home point, warp to use an inn, and warp back. That would respawn enemies; this option does not.)
Max Level Up:Increases the party's maxium level, enabling further grinding to reduce difficulty. The maximum level is configurable. (60, 70, 80, 90, 99).
Easier Non-Bosses:Decreases the difficulty of non-boss enemies down to one difficulty below the current active difficulty. Bosses are unaffected.
Custom Difficulty:Enables freely adjusting the difficulty either up or down. (Normally you can only set it down from where it currently is.)
Skip Minigames:Enables the option to skip minigames and obtain an automatic placement. (This enables an automatic first-place in Salmon Racing and Quintar Racing.)
Extend Timers:Adds more time to timers which sometimes show up while solving puzzles.
Boost EXP:Increases the amount of EXP earned after battle. The exact percentage is configurable. (100%-300%, in 10% increments.)
Boost LXP:Increases the amount of LXP earned after battle. The exact percentage is configurable. (100%-300%, in 10% increments.)
Boost Gold:Increases the amount of Gold earned after battle. The exact percentage is configurable. (100%-300%, in 10% increments.)

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Challenge Options.value:
Pressing a button during game creation will yield the following configurable options:
Game Mode:Standard, vanilla (revert to original release, omitting balance changes from patches), or chaos (???, also disables some assist options)
Member Limit:1-4 party members
Max Level Limit:1-60
No Assist Options:On/off. Disables Assist Options.
No Telegraphs:On/off. Disables previewing enemy intent.
No Class Change:On/off. Disables changing Classes.
No Sub-Command: On/off. Disables setting Sub-Commands
Hardcore:On/off. Defeat means the end of adventure.
EXP Rate:0-100%. Decreases the amount of EXP earned after battle.
LXP Rate:0-100%. Decreases the amount of LXP earned after battle.
Gold Rate:0-100%. Decreases the amount of Gold earned after battle.
Randomizer Options: See separate section.

Section: New Game Plus.value:
After you complete the game, you will be returned to the game at the Spawning Point in Spawning Meadows. If you talk to the Nan present there, you will be asked if you want to start your journey over. This initiates a New Game Plus mode.
All of these selections are yes/no choices.
Keep Crystals:
Keep Levels:
Keep Learned Abilities:
Keep Gold:
Keep Equipment:
Limitless Equipment:Enables acquiring multiple copies of equipment that is normally limited in capacity. Note: This is an Assist Option.
Keep Consumables:
Keep Instruments:
Keep Teleport Stones:
Keep Pouches:
Keep Maps:
Keep Revealed areas:
Keep Hatchery:
Keep Archive:
You will then be prompted with challenge, randomizer, and difficulty choices. You will then be dropped into a new game at Spawning Meadows.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Randomizer Options.value:
For choices, between scaled and full, scaled randomizes with those of similar power or importance. Full completely randomizes them.
Random Crystals:On/off. Randomizes Crystal locations and the initial six Classes.
Random Monsters:Off/scaled/full. Randomizes the non-boss Flame encounters.
Random Bosses:Off/scaled/full. Randomizes boss encounters.
Random Items: Off/scaled/full. Randomizes item locations.
Include Basic Items: On/off. Includes basic/recovery items (eg, Potions, Ethers, Scrolls) in randomized item locations.
Include Quest Items: On/off. Includes quest-related items (eg, Black Squirrels, Dog Bones, Lost Penguins) in randomized item locations.
Include Progression: On/off. Includes Tools and progression-related Key Items in randomized item locations.
Random Equipment: Off/scaled/full. Randomizes equipment locations.
Random Class Abilities:Off/on/free. Randomizes which abilities can be learned by which Classes except for Monster Magic and Summon Magic. (On randomizes only to Classes that are capable of using them. Free completely randomizes them and ability weapon restrictions are removed.)
Include Monster Magic: On/off. Includes Monster Magic in randomized Class abilities.
Include Summon Magic: On/off. Includes Summon Magic in randomized Class abilities.
Random Enemy Abilities:On/off. Randomizes which abilities can be used by which enemies.
Random Passives:On/off. Randomizes which passive abilities can be learned by which Classes.
Random Innate Passives:On/off. Randomzies which innate passive abilities are attached to which Classes.
Random Warp Points:On/off. Randomizes the spawn point and teleport locations.
Random Music: On/off. Randomizes music.
Progression Gate: On/off. Castle Sequoia cannot be accessed until all Crystals have been discovered. The location of the New World Stone will not be randomized.
Get Home Point Stone:On/off. Begins the adventure with a Home Point Stone already in your inventory.
Get Treasure Finder:On/off. Begins the adventure with the Treasure Finder already in your inventory.
Get All Maps:On/off. Begins the adventure with all maps already in your inventory.
Spoiler Log:On/off. Enables access to the Spoiler Log to see where Tools and progression-related Key Items have been randomized to. (Requires Randomize Items and Include Progression to be on.)
Seed:Choose the randomizer seed. Using the same seed will result in the same random output.

Description.value: In Crystal Project, your primary means of fast travel involves using a Home Point Crystal to teleport to a floating cube-shaped crystal that's set as your Home Point, of which your designated Home Point can be adjusted to any one of these crystals. However, there is another means of fast travel via one-use shards and multi-use stones linked to specific Shrines throughout the game world.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Callisto Shrine.value: Sitting atop the southern edge of the desolate Land's End, the shrine is at one of the highest points in the continent, and can be used as a launching point to easily travel to the lands below in any direction with a capable mount. The shrine is not maintained by anyone due to its remote location, though your party may find the multi-use obsidian stone somewhere atop the shrine itself.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Dione Shrine.value:
Dione Shrine
Nestled within a cliff at the very north of the Quintar Reserve, the shrine is seemingly maintained by intelligent Quintar that use the shrine as a nursery, and will entertain human visitors capable of communicating with them. It is likely that your party may end up discovering the shrine long before you are able to communicate with the Quintar, so the multi-use stone may not be immediately available. There are several one-use Dione Shards strewn about, but in the case you run out, a certain lost and found at Capital Sequoia may have extras for you to use. The price of the multi-use fluorite stone to warp to this shrine is 4 .

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Europa Shrine.value: Hiding beneath the northern jungle of the Jidamba Tangle, the shrine is seemingly attended by one of the only humans present on the vast jungle island, of which the shrine itself appears to be popular with the local birds. The price for the multi-use emerald stone to warp to this shrine is 2 .

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Gaea Shrine.value: The first shrine that your party will usually encounter, it is the only shrine located within actual civilization in the land of Sequoia, within Capital Sequoia itself. The price for the multi-use grey-colored stone to warp to this shrine is 2 .

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Ganymede Shrine.value:
Ganymede Shrine
This shrine sits upon the northwestern cliffs overlooking the farms atop Shoudu Province. Reaching the shrine usually involves jumping on fences in order to climb onto the pipes leading into the cliffs where the shrine resides. The price for the multi-use topaz stone to warp to this shrine is 1 .

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Mars Shrine.value: Resting in the midwestern section of the Poko Poko Desert, this shrine is strangely broken down and abandoned. It is very likely that your party may discover the multi-use ruby stone that whisks them to the shrine before actually finding the shrine itself. Exactly how the stone ended up so far away from Mars Shrine or the reason for the shrine's current state is a great mystery.

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Mercury Shrine.value:
Mercury Shrine
This shrine is located on a mountainside that borders the regions of the Spawning Meadows to the west, Delende to the north, Seaside Cliffs to the east, and Beaurior Volcano to the south.
It is possible for your party to discover this shrine before reaching Capital Sequoia. Reach it from Delende by jumping south from the first tree on the right from Spawning Meadows, and pressing against the cliff as you go around it west then south. Or, reach it from the western entrance of the Seaside Cliffs, by remaining as far west as possible, jumping over gaps and rivers until you are able to scale the mountainside where the shrine lies.
The price for the multi-use bronze-colored stone to warp to this shrine is 10 .

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Neptune Shrine.value:
Neptune Shrine
A small distance southwest off the coast of the Sara Sara Bazaar, the shrine rests submerged under the surface, maintained by a singular, solitary person. Prospective explorers of the deep would need to have the proper tools to reach here. Though a strange place for a shrine to be, it must serve some proper use to adventurers. The price of the multi-use amethyst stone to warp to this shrine is 4 .

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Poseidon Shrine.value:
Poseidon Shrine
Located near the source of the Salmon River, up above the cabin where Salmon are being raised by a group of bears to participate in an activity known as the Salmon Run. The easiest way to reach the shrine is to participate in the Salmon Run at least once, in which you are rewarded with a Poseidon Shard regardless of your placement that can be used to teleport to the shrine above. The price for the multi-use sapphire stone to warp to this shrine is 15 .

sources.applicability: Community wiki evidence; Nintendo Switch and enabled-mod applicability are unverified

Section: Triton Shrine.value: Overlooking the strange tall wooden fence separating northwestern Tall, Tall Heights from the southwestern section, the most direct route to reaching the shrine involves thinking of the fence as a bridge instead. If one climbs the tree to the ledge on the eastern side of the fence, they can walk on the fence thereafter to cross over to where Triton Shrine lies. The price for the multi-use teal-colored stone to warp to this shrine is 1 50 .

Section: Lure Locations.value:
Plug Lure can be found in the fountain in Capital Sequoia.
Fly Lure can be obtained from Chloe on the walls overlooking capital courtyard. Rent a Quintar in Rolling Quintar Fields, go south, jump onto the wall (you need to make it to the wall, not just the ledge). Run over to the Courtyard gate to where there are two lamps on either side 4 spaces apart. Get a running start and jump over with the Quintar. For an easier time, wait until you have the Quintar flute and climb onto the wall from alley east of the Weary Wanderer's Lodge.
Jiggling Lure can be found in the Northeast corner of Shoudu Province, on the narrow pathways. A short cut-scene with Chloe and Talon will occur and then the player will receive the lure. If the NPCs are not present, check with them near the end of the Salmon River race to prompt them to travel to Shoudu.

Description.value:
Explore the world, find Crystals, and fulfill the prophecy to bring balance to the land of Sequoia.
...Or maybe you'd rather spend your time collecting neat equipment and artifacts? Or tame strange creatures and fill out all the entries in your archive? Or perhaps you'd rather hunt down every monster and conquer the world's toughest bosses. Or maybe you'd rather travel to the farthest reaches of the land and uncover the world's greatest mysteries.
The choice is yours, as it should be! Or is it? They say that those who stray out of line will be punished, killed, or worse. Maybe it's for your own good that you stick to collecting Crystals, just like everyone else. But where would the adventure be in that?
